method: Checked the claims associated with every numbered reference against primary legislation, agency guidance, official statistics, original reporting, publisher abstracts or author manuscripts. Direct HTTP status is recorded separately from whether the source content was readable through the web reader. Public sources were submitted to Wayback after their claim checks. Only service-confirmed captures are linked.
limitations: Publisher bot challenges do not necessarily indicate broken links. Where a DOI destination was challenged, an accessible author manuscript or publisher abstract was used, as specified in the per-reference verification.
Full paywalled academic papers and the full subscriber-only Focus Taiwan report were not used when only abstracts or a headline/lead were available.

Wayback replay URLs returned connection-refused errors in this environment. New capture links are based on successful Save Page Now responses; older captures are based on CDX records reporting HTTP 200. Replay rendering could not be independently verified.

removed_or_replaced_sources.change: Removed an uncited, generic MOI FAQ page; retained its legacy anchor with the relevant NIA guidance. No article claim was removed.
Replaced inaccessible China Times/CNA reprint with the Ministry of Justice court-judgment digest.
Replaced DOI link resolving to a publisher 404 with the University of Portsmouth repository; retained DOI text as a bibliographic identifier.
Replaced failing HTTP links with working HTTPS versions.
